### Care Services and Public Health Training

::: {.section-card}
#### Demand for care services in online vacancies

Using KZiS-aligned occupation codes (care and social-work families), we identify **~1,100 postings** in 2025 that signal direct care-service delivery — a narrow slice of Pracuj.pl dominated by **medical care assistants**, **elderly-care workers** and related roles. A broader text-and-title classifier surfaces roughly **14,200** postings when clinical and therapeutic occupations are included.

Employer concentration is **high** in both segments: the top 10 employers account for roughly **half** of care-tagged offers, compared with a more fragmented market in general healthcare NACE postings.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-block">
  <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 35.</strong> Top care-related occupations by posting volume (KZiS-mapped titles, 2025)</div>
  <div id="chart-care-top-occupations" class="plotly-chart plotly-chart--wide" role="img" aria-label="Top care-related occupations on Pracuj.pl"></div>
  <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> Direct care demand captured by Pracuj.pl is small and concentrated in a limited set of occupations. This likely understates broader care-sector demand, especially in public and municipal services.</p>
</div>
<p class="notes source-note">Source: Pracuj.pl 2025; KZiS-mapped occupation titles.</p>
```
:::

::: {.section-card}
#### Skills profile of care-related offers

Care postings emphasise **assisting & caring (S3)** and **management (S4)** more than the general healthcare NACE sample, while **ICT (S5)** is less prominent — reflecting hands-on and coordination tasks rather than hospital IT roles. Top requested skills include **computer literacy**, **management skills** and **elderly care**; knowledge demand centres on **paramedical practice** and **nursing science**.

```{=html}

    <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> Care-related postings combine hands-on care skills with general digital and management skills. This suggests that even direct care roles increasingly require coordination and basic administrative capabilities.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chart-block">
    <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 37.</strong> Top knowledge concepts in care-related offers</div>
    <div id="chart-care-top-knowledge" class="plotly-chart" role="img" aria-label="Top knowledge in care offers"></div>
    <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> Knowledge demand in care postings centres on paramedical practice and nursing-related knowledge. This confirms that care work often requires occupation-specific knowledge, not only generic empathy or assistance skills.</p>
```
